checkpoints.label: Foundations
checkpoints.goal: Solve basic arrays/hashing/two pointers independently; explain Big O and HTTP request flow

checkpoints.label: Core DSA
checkpoints.goal: Binary search without boundary bugs, recursive tree traversals, basic LLD and concurrency vocabulary

checkpoints.label: Graphs
checkpoints.goal: Choose BFS/DFS/DSU/topological sort/Dijkstra appropriately; design basic scalable systems

checkpoints.label: DP + HLD
checkpoints.goal: Derive DP states and recurrences; discuss failures, concurrency, trade-offs and service architecture

checkpoints.label: Interview baseline
checkpoints.goal: Unseen medium in ~35–45 min; coherent 40-min design mock; portfolio MVP and active applications

checkpoints.label: Application conversion
checkpoints.goal: Run targeted applications, improve from feedback, maintain mocks, aim for written offer before resignation

rules: DSA without Copilot: clarify → examples → brute force → optimize → C# → dry run → Big-O.
Study the Dometrain foundation, then only selected Educative examples, then separate unseen LeetCode problems.
Record Independent / Hints / Solution Needed. Repeat difficult problems after 2 days, 1 week and 3 weeks.
Friday and Saturday remain system design days. Keep one small lab/design exercise every week.
CounterNet is a scoped systems lab, not a second full-time project. Cut project scope before interview practice.
Targets are readiness indicators, not proof of senior-level production experience.
Prioritize real SWE work achievements and accurate behavioral stories; do not inflate QA work into dev ownership.
Apply from April; resign only after a suitable written offer.
